This behavior raises two connected questions. What state supports exact
repair without rereading the surviving raw corpus? How much information can

This behavior raises two connected questions. What state supports exact
repair without rereading the surviving raw corpus? How much information can
future deletions require about examples excluded today? For this curator,
the remaining deletion budget determines which records can still enter
training. Payloads that cannot become eligible can be discarded permanently
within that budget. The construction below shows the converse possibility:
one additional allowed deletion can make every private sign of the excluded

edits.before:
We make three scoped contributions. First, we specialize signed Boolean
provenance to the ordered curator and derive a summary that repairs both
training statistics and its own designated algebraic state. Second, we give
a finite-format construction linking excluded feature bits to exact ridge
heads, including a sharp change in required private information when the
deletion horizon increases by one. Third, we report two completed, negative
calibrations for a fully LLM natural-text study. Neither admitted a threshold
under its frozen model-agreement criterion. The downstream comparison of
target changes, utility, and complete system cost remains unexecuted.
A separately declared structural follow-up characterizes all 51 score graphs
on a fixed natural development panel without selecting a cutoff.
edits.after:
We make three scoped contributions. First, we specialize signed Boolean
provenance to obtain an exact summary of additive training statistics whose
updated state equals reconstruction at the remaining deletion horizon.
Second, we construct finite-format features shared by the curator and ridge
learner for which that horizon determines an exact private-information
minimum, attained by a sequential codec. Third, we report two negative
calibrations for a fully LLM natural-text study. Neither selected a threshold
under its frozen model-defined criterion, so the downstream comparison of
target changes, utility, and complete system cost remains unexecuted.
Separate development diagnostics characterize all 51 score graphs and check
exact membership repair without selecting a cutoff.

edits.reason: Credit direct antecedents and tighten contribution boundary
edits.before:
Neither deletion-induced additions nor provenance maintenance is a new
general principle. Nonmonotone database queries already exhibit the former,
and provenance and incremental view maintenance address the latter
\citep{green,aggregate,dbsp,priu,ivmunlearning}. Our claim concerns the stated curator,
remaining-horizon repair contract, and shared-feature learner construction.
The results are useful when specifying an unlearning service: its target,
remaining deletion budget, and access to excluded data determine what it must
retain. They do not establish that a polynomial summary is the cheapest
implementation. In particular, a compact eligible-payload baseline can use
less total memory. The negative calibration also shows why a theoretical
repair guarantee should not be presented as validated semantic deduplication.
Whether natural-text target changes justify the complete repair cost remains
an open empirical question.
edits.after:
Deletion-induced additions and provenance maintenance are established in
nonmonotone queries and incremental computation
\citep{green,aggregate,dbsp,priu,ivmunlearning}. Summary-based unlearning
across feature selection and model fitting also precedes this work
\citep{cao}. So do definitions that include metadata for subsequent deletions
and distinguish internal state from one released output \citep{ginart,cohencontrol}.
Our results specify one ordered curator, its remaining-horizon coefficient
map, and a shared-feature ridge construction. They make the target, allowed
future requests, and access to excluded data part of an explicit storage
contract. They do not establish a practical memory advantage: a compact
eligible-payload baseline can use less total memory. Whether natural-text
target changes justify the complete repair cost remains unresolved.

edits.reason: Document complete frozen tokenization/pooling/precision recipe
edits.before: \paragraph{Asset attribution and replay limits.}
edits.after:
\paragraph{Full-document embedding recipe.}\label{app:embedding}
Content is tokenized once without special tokens or truncation and split
into consecutive blocks of at most 256 content tokens. Separately tokenized
\texttt{query: } IDs are prepended to each block before the tokenizer adds
special tokens; content is never decoded and retokenized. For the pinned
E5 tokenizer, chunks are padded to 261 tokens. Batches contain chunks of
one document only. The encoder runs in evaluation mode on CPU in FP32,
with eager attention and deterministic algorithms enabled. Pooling masks
padding and averages all attended tokens, including prefix and special
tokens. Each FP32 mean is normalized using coordinate-ordered FP64 norm
accumulation. In document order, normalized chunk vectors are weighted by
their content-token counts and accumulated in FP64. Their weighted mean
is normalized again and cast to the stored FP32 row. Cosine scoring
renormalizes those stored rows in FP64. The supplement provides the exact
embedding and scoring source; the model card alone does not specify this
full-document procedure. Absolute scores and the failed calibration are
conditional on this fixed recipe, not a conclusion about every use of E5.
